Aqueo™ is a versatile display sans serif inspired by the cylindrical wireframe of a water glass. It comes in 6 weights, 12 styles, and 1,350 glyphs each. 

Aqueo™ fonts feature an extra set of stylistic alternates; The standard uppercase set takes more traditional forms, while the alternate uppercase set sports unorthodox lowercase forms. The standards exude confidence and dependability yet are friendly and approachable, and the alternates elicit more fun, quirky and whimsical. Aqueo™ comes loaded with Opentype features such as case-sensitive marks, punctuations and mathematic symbols. It also has an extensive set of discretionary ligatures, stylistic alternates, and over 80 UX/UI icons.

A liminal work, Aptly addresses the condition in which humanity may be expressed under the normalizing constraints of technocratic systems. To this end, Aptly’s design space is posited as an array of severe constraints which demand an aesthetic resolution. The resolving concept is “Geo-Soft”, characters being constructed from arcs of circle connected by orthogonal straight lines, with few diagonals and nary a sharp corner—as if words are being routed by a bit of fixed dimension. The effect has an engaging tension, with soft edges offsetting rigorous structure, as if words are simultaneously melting and compiling. Working this conceptual template, Aptly fashions a cool, elemental repose.

Apparat introduces subtle humanistic touches into what is essentially a geometric design. While the typeface retains the appeal of simple geometric shapes like circles and straight lines, squares and triangles, the “humanised” characters increase the distinction between specific letters, thus improving the typeface’s legibility. This approach takes cues from W.A. Dwiggins’ Metro. The seminal Art Deco design sought to improve on the new wave of geometric sans serifs appearing in the early twentieth century. Apparat’s humanised letterforms retain a sharpness that harmonises perfectly with the triangular letters and crisp stroke endings. The font family comes in 4 widths, each in eleven weights

Apolline family was designed to study the transition from Renaissance writing into the first printing types. It is an exploration of design methods used by people like Nicolas Jenson for adapting handwriting with its multiple occurrences. Jean François Porchez drawings were modelled after his own calligraphy at a small size (2 cm high for the capitals) to preserve the irregularity of human handwriting. The serifs were designed asymmetrically to reinforce the rhythm of the writing. The final drawings were produced at a large size (10 cm high for the capitals) to allow for subtle optimisation. The initial drawings were digitised with Ikarus to create the final roman and italic fonts.

Apocalypso's name [from apocalypse -the end of the world, and calypso -joyful improvised music] is analogous to ‘fiddling while Rome burns’. The pictograms and crosses are considered an art project more than a practical font, yet the crosses add decorative detailing to typographic layouts, while the pictograms can be used to great effect on t-shirts or for other graphic matter. Apocalypso is a document of our time and a scarily prophetic vision of our dystopian future.

A classic text face with interesting details, giving it lots of character. Anziano does show touches of another classic typeface – Weiss (by Emil Rudolf Weiss, 1926). Extra flavour is added with symbols and ornaments.

Antona is a basic and neutral geometric font family with 16 styles (384 glyphs each). Its appearance is rather neutral; vertical stroke endings and fairly large apertures make for an open, friendly character. Antona comes balanced spacing & kerning and well-adjusted obliques—easy on the eyes in display sizes and also in body copy.

Antarctican hybridizes ruler and compass geometry and American wood type.  Asymmetric contrast, deep notches, and a tall x-height aid legibility at small sizes and demand attention when set large. Text styles are monospaced and headlines styles are proportionally spaced. This allows text to challenge convention while the headlines can be set in weights ranging from thin to ultrablack.

Support for over 200 languages allows Antarctican to set type for international readerships. OpenType niceties include small caps, lining, superior and inferior numbers, prebuilt fractions in monospaced fonts and arbitrary fractions in headline fonts, and f ligatures.

Anisette is built around the idea of two widths capitals and can be described as a geometric sanserif typeface. It is influenced by the 30s and the Art Deco movement. A simple sentence set in Anisette will be extremely diverse in its representations, due of the the number of Anisette variables. Indeed, the wide and narrow capitals can alternatively be used alone, mixed manually since the early days of Anisette. With Anisette, typography becomes a game, to design any title page will as flamboyant as if Anisette has been specially drawn for it.

Anisette Petite can be described as a geometric sans serif typeface influenced by the 30s and the Art-Déco movement. In France, at that time, the Art-Déco spirit was mainly capitals. Therefore, adding lowercases, the story became more complicated. His stylistic references couldn’t anymore be restricted to the French Art-Déco period. The references expanded to include shop signs present in our cities throughout the twentieth century. The outcome of this Anisette Petite; a palette of slightly strange shapes, that does not strictly follow the geometrical, mechanical or historical principles. Anisette Petite capitals are designed a square proportions, to mix with narrow and wide Anisette caps.

Angus hand is a set of authentic handwriting fonts remincent of a time before computers when sending hand-written letters was part of our daily lives. Based on samples of love letters written from Victoria, Canada in 1955—Angus Hand subtly conveys the love and care that was written into the content of those original letters. 

Angus hand is based on the handwriting of my grandfather R.B.Angus. I traced the original letters he wrote to my nana and those drawings served as the casual style, which stays true to the imperfections that bring warmth to these letterforms. I then created a calligraphy style for a slightly more formal version of my grandfather’s writing.

A lot of the handwriting-style fonts I make are more on the childlike side. For this one, I wanted to go a bit more adult, but still keep the fun vibe. And so, here's Angry Potato!  It's a casual handwriting font with both uppercase and lowercase; a bit on the taller and narrower side, with a slightly varying stroke weight. 

Smooth for cutting, stylish for print, it's a font that can do it all: logos and branding, packaging, fun designs on shirts or mugs, digital designs, social media, book titles, videos, games, and more!

Angie Sans is a low contrast incised sans serif that shares some similarities with Optima by Hermann Zapf and Pascal by José Mendoza (both created at the end of the 50’s). Angie Sans italics are based on Chancery forms from the Renaissance, and is narrower than the roman shapes.

Angie Sans is an extremely legible typeface; thanks to it Roman proportioned capitals, open counter lower cases and strong horizontals.The manual gesture present in Angie Sans, offers plastic qualities such as warmth, craftmanship and humanity. Available in six series, with matching italics, Angie Sans work well in design projects that require delicate and human touch.

With the same characteristics of the Anadiego family, Anadiego Rounded arrives full of warmth and rounded shapes as its name indicates. 
AnaDiego Rounded is a display sans-serif typeface that sets itself apart with tight closures between closed letters like “c,” “e,” “s,” and “a.” Giving it a unique personality and setting it apart from the common shapes of other sans-serif fonts.
It is a perfect choice for texts, titles, subtitles, labels, and any text that requires a striking presence.

AnaDiego, an exceptional typeface, is a heartfelt tribute to Ana Teresa Diego, an Argentine astronomy student who tragically disappeared in 1976. This unique font boasts distinctive features, such as tight closures between letters 'c,' 'e,' 's,' and 'a,' setting it apart from traditional sans-serif fonts. Its condensed and narrow design allows for efficient use of space, making it the perfect choice for large texts, titles, subtitles, labels, and any content that demands a bold presence. With six weights – Thin, ExtraLight, Light, Regular, Medium, and Bold – and a character set comprising 725 letters, including support for Vietnamese, AnaDiego offers a versatile toolkit for designers.

Amulet evolved after a trip to Dublin, Ireland. It has a Celtic calligraphic influence which must have subconsciously come from looking at ancient manuscripts and the Book of Kells in Trinity College.
Amulet is a distinctive headline font with gaelic roots, ideal for posters, film titles and guaranteed to lend your designs a scribal, monastic look and feel.
An uncial font with a twist, Amulet has a definite air of spiritual mysticism about it and in a certain light an almost Arabic flavour.

Amorie has three different font styles; Modella (classic and chic), Nova (fun and fancy) or SC (Small Caps and all business). Each style comes in light, medium and bold and has an accompanying italics version.

Amorie includes a large set of graphic extras, including stylish frames, arrows, line breaks, corners, flourishes and more. The complete package gives you one unbeatable font family.

Austrian Cartoonist Wolfgang Ammer lent his handwriting to create this font produced by the team at Schriftlabor. Wolfgang uses the font in his daily routine: It facilitates corrections and translations of his cartoons for international newspapers.
It is a script typeface that includes rich in contextual alternates. Ammer contains about 1800 glyphs, and each character has multiple alternative shapes. We wrote a complex OpenType substitution feature that makes sure that the same variant does not appear twice in a line. It has a lot of character and shows a fast and spontaneous feeling to it.

Wood type seen through a new lens.
Americane is not based on any single existing wood type style, it is actually a combination of the most salient styles of Von Döhren’s survey of the American wood type landscape, applied to a broad use type family. Starting with the lightest weights, the designer’s sensitivity to form delivers a lightline more representative of metal gothics of the period, exhibiting also a subtle dynamism in the curves. Toward Americane’s heavy end, its true character shows, as it is here that the idiosyncratic texture peculiar to wood type begins to emerge. The result is something new that’s still evocative of type you can hold in your hand.

Ambroise is a contemporary interpretation of various typefaces belonging to Didot’s late style, conceived circa 1830. Ambroise attempts to reproduce what we see on 19th century printed paper; a more accurate representation of Didot punches. The unbracketed serif uses tiny transitional curves instead of the true square straight-line forms. The result is a softer and less straight appearance on the page, particularly at larger sizes. Every variation of the typeface carries a name in homage to a member of type founders and printers in the illustrious Didot family. The condensed variant is called Ambroise Firmin. The extra-condensed is called Ambroise François.

Uppercase? Lowercase? Why not both?! Ambicase is an award-winning conceptual display type that combines traditional upper- and lowercase forms within the same letters. Somehow both familiar and alien, the forms of the Ambicase typefaces toy with inherited assumptions about letterforms. Ambicase Modern was the inaugural release from Teeline Fonts; Ambicase Fatface cranks up the weight and contrast.

Amberwood is a merging of sans serif and blackletter style letterforms. With a unique blend of deliberate curves and a solid stance on the baseline, it resembles tall trees in a dense wood. This font exudes a whimsical yet sophisticated charm that’s perfect for making enchanting projects. Whether you’re designing a fairy tale book cover, crafting a fantasy logo, or creating eye-catching packaging for food or beer, this font will add a touch of “ye olde awesome” to your designs. Its slender form makes it ideal for headlines, titles, and logos, and its distinctive character gives your text a unique and creative edge.

Amareddine is an Arabic branding typeface designed by Nadine Chahine. The family has 7 weights ranging from Thin to Black and offers a lot of flexibility for design work and in a variety of applications. Its design is a Naskh-Kufi hybrid and is suited for headlines, UI, advertising, and branding. The overall feeling is friendly and approachable, with a contemporary look and feel. The fonts support Arabic language and have proportional and tabular numerals. Amareddine is part of the 2020: After the Fall collection.

Alverata is a contemporary, eclectic font family inspired by type from medieval Europe. Capital inscriptions are the basis for this face, which can be seen in its short, thorn-like serifs and flared forms. Alverata also experiments with the characters themselves by exchanging straight lines for curves and vice versa, becoming resolutely modern in the process. Alverata performs beautifully in both digital and physical applications, delivering excellent openness and legibility in small text and proving lively and attractive at large sizes.

Altesse is a typographic adaptation of the scripts engraved by the French copperplate masters from the 19th and 20th centuries. Free from the constraints of metal type, Altesse is designed in two optical sizes, allowing you to rediscover the pleasure of automated calligraphy. With the arrival of copperplate engraving and printing, which gradually replaced the usual uses of calligraphy, typographic styles that imitate writing developed separately from italics. Altesse is not the revival of a particular reference; it is a contemporary interpretation of various nineteenth-century engraved sources. Its designs are directly influenced by the French copperplate engravings in use over the centuries

name: Alphazet
authors: Mirela Belova, Stan Partalev, Luboslav Boyanov

raw.designer: Mirela Belova, Stan Partalev, Luboslav Boyanov
raw.description:
Alphazet includes 9 weights (Thin to Black), each accompanied by matching oblique italics. The typeface is available in standard OTF, TTF, and web formats and as a single variable font file. Alphazet supports over 220 languages, covering Extended Latin, Cyrillic, and Greek scripts. OpenType features include ligatures, stylistic sets, contextual alternates, tabular figures, fractions, ordinals, and case-sensitive forms. 

Alphazet’s design is suitable for a variety of uses. The typeface's tall x-height and good spacing make it easy to read, so it’s perfect for body text. It also has a strong, balanced look that works well in headlines and posters.

This is the variable version of Almandin typeface, which contains 7 basic weights and corresponding italics.

Almandin is a slightly calligraphic sans, influenced by our years studying at the École Estienne, where calligraphy was central. We had to rise to the challenge of creating a sans that was both neutral enough to be used in many contexts, and at the same time highly recognisable. Robert Slimbach's work, particularly on Cronos, was an important reference. Almandin contains many stylistic variations and its width remains constant whatever the weight chosen.

Almandin is available in a choice of 7 static weights or 1 variable version.

Allumi Inline, reaffirms by its design, a humanized technological and scientific universe. Pushed to their limits, neither perfectly round nor geometrically square, the shapes of the Allumi Inline embody a human vision of the high-tech universe.

The concept is an inline drawn in italic in a Roman shape. The result is a dynamic that plays on the optics and creates visual surprises. While a retro effect usually emerges in the Inline variants, the sloping design reinforces the idea of precision, of technological mastery. Allumi inline is offered in two optical variants.

Allumi is a different font. Different from anything Jean François Porchez has designed in the past. Allumi is a sleek typeface designed with technology in mind. It is a perfect font family for any communication in design, robotics, or functionality. It is a human design with a high tech touch. Allumi's unique design and sturdy forms makes it a serious typeface. Its pure shapes weaves a global presence today with an outlook to the future.

The Allumi family has been built around two series of widths, standard and extended. Italics have been carefully designed as slanted roman with all necessary optical and human corrections to create a perfect and neat italic.

Allrounder Monument is an inscriptional, dignified member of the Allrounder superfamily. This all-caps typeface with delicate serifs was inspired by ancient Roman inscriptions. It infuses today’s designs with a hint of history and an air of exclusivity.
A timeless titling typeface, it’s great for posters, magazines, book covers, greeting cards, advertising, and packaging. Discretionary Ligatures and Stylistic Alternates provide make for an even more spectacular look.
Allrounder Monument consists of three weights with almost 600 glyphs each. Its vertical metrics and texture match those of the other Allrounder typefaces: Combining fonts was never easier than with the Allrounder type system.

Allrounder Grotesk Mono is a non-proportional typeface that adapts the rational modernist letterforms of Allrounder Grotesk. While a monospace font is never the most versatile instrument in your typographic toolbox, the neutral shapes of Allrounder Grotesk Mono will ensure you can use it for literature magazines, hipster art brandings, code, final reminders—and much, much more. If there is such a thing as a monospace workhorse, this is it.
Allrounder Grotesk Mono consists of five weights from Light to Bold with 580+ glyphs per font. Its vertical metrics and texture match those of the other Allrounder typefaces: Combining fonts was never easier than with the Allrounder type system.

Allrounder Grotesk is a neutral, powerful neogrotesk from the Allrounder superfamily. An unobtrusive teamplayer as well as an excellent soloist, this workhorse is ready for anything from even body text to crisp and clean headlines—in annual reports, editorial design, books, branding, packaging, large-scale ads, forms, or posters.
Allrounder Grotesk consists of ten weights ranging from Air to Black with 900+ glyphs each and hand-corrected obliques. Its vertical metrics and texture match those of the other Allrounder typefaces: Combining fonts was never easier than with the Allrounder type system.
(i) Allrounder Grotesk was heavily updated in 2024. v2.0 is not compatible with older versions.

Allrounder Didone is a refined modern/classicist serif typeface from the Allrounder superfamily especially suited to fashion and culture as well as legal and scientific topics. Like the original designs by 18th/19th-century masters such as Didot, Bodoni, and Walbaum, Allrounder Didone comes in optical sizes, each with 12 styles and ~950 glyphs per font. The classic “Allrounder Didone” family is great for all-purpose typesetting even in small captions. In larger sizes, it makes headlines appear strong and confident. For the true high-contrast Didone look, we added “Allrounder Didone Big”. They can be employed solo, together, or combined with any other font from the Allrounder type system.

Allrounder Baroque is a transitional serif member of the Allrounder superfamily. A playful and dynamic medium-contrast typeface, its lush shapes guide the reader’s eye across the page.
Like its famous Baroque-era ancestors penned by van Dijck, Fleischmann, and Baskerville, Allrounder Baroque is an ideal book typeface. Set large, it’s at home in luxury branding and serious-yet-approachable corporate design.
At 10 styles and 900+ glyphs, with extended language support and OpenType features, Allrounder Baroque brings workhorse qualities to the table. Its vertical metrics and texture match those of the other Allrounder fonts: Combining fonts was never easier than with the Allrounder type system.

Allrounder Antiqua is an old-style serif member of the Allrounder superfamily. A timeless typeface based on classical proportions, it’s perfectly suitable for advanced book and editorial design as well as packaging and branding.
Loosely modeled on Robert Granjon's “Ascendonica Romain” from 1567, its main purpose is to set flawless body copy—but its refined shapes work fantastically in display applications, too.
This classy serif typeface comes in four weights with corresponding true italics and plenty of OpenType features. Its vertical metrics and texture match those of the other Allrounder typefaces: Combining fonts was never easier than with the Allrounder type system.

Allegory is a connecting script font with a ton of swoop, bounce, and flair!  It's hand-drawn, and extensively cleaned up so that it's smooth and sleek at any size.

The base alphabet starts out fun, but then things get even more exciting when you look at the alternates and ligatures.  There are over 65 multi-letter ligatures to make sure letters flow well into each other, and over 100 alternate characters so you can add variety and flourish to your design.  (And of course, everything is properly PUA-encoded for super easy access.)

Designed to harmonize between three scripts – Latin, Cyrillic, and Greek, Alkes is a contemporary yet well-defined humanist serif that combines the best out of the digital and analog worlds.

Featuring a generous x-height, wide letter spacing, large open counters, and angled stress contrast, Alkes is highly effective for editorials and publishing, where long texts and legibility are the key forces. Its attractive details, calligraphic structure, and asymmetrical serifs shine through larger sizes and make Alkes suitable for headlines.

Alkes has a pull with editorial designers, graphic designers, and publishers who aim for a clear structure, hierarchy, and coherent non-Latin scripts.

Alio™ Text is a workhorse typeface which works beautifully as the display type, body copy and anything in between. We redesigned Alio Text with taller x-height, more pronounced accents, and wider letter spacing than its sibling, Alio™ Pro. We also cut down from 6 weights/12 styles to 4 weights/8 styles to ensure legibility and readability and to maximize the weight contrast at small sizes. Alio Text supports most Latin-based languages and packs with Open-Type features similar to Alio Pro. If you’re looking for a go-to, versatile typeface for most occasions, Alio Text is for you. (4 weights/8 font styles, 500+ glyphs each).

Alio™– Let Your Creativity Flow. 

Inspired by sleek sans serifs and flowing cursives, Alio™ features the best of both worlds. This display type's hybrid modular design gives you many alternates and options to play. Just let your creativity flow and enjoy creating a wide range of styles from minimalistic modern to decorative flourish. When combining this display type with Alio Decor, you can let your creativity flow to the max. You can create stunning flourish designs and unique type treatments for your projects. 

Alio Decor is more than just an Alio Pro’s sidekick. You can enjoy creating flourish designs exclusively with Alio Decor. [6 weights/12 font styles, 300+ glyphs each].

Inspired by sleek sans serifs and flowing cursives, Alio™ features the best of both worlds. Just let your creativity flow and enjoy creating a broad range of styles from minimalistic modern to decorative flourish. By combining Alio™ Pro with Alio™ Decor, you can create stunning flourish designs and unique type treatments for your projects.

Alio™ Pro comes loaded with extensive alternates & ligatures. The Pro also supports most Latin-based languages. [6 weights/12 font styles. 750+ glyphs each]  

Alio Decor is more than just an Alio Pro’s sidekick. You can enjoy creating flourish designs exclusively with Alio Decor. [6 weights/12 font styles, 300+ glyphs each].

Alimentary is a font family that's taller, narrower, with a hip and retro feel. When I finished the Medium weight, I felt like I wanted a Light weight. Then a Heavy weight. Then I figured, "what the heck," and made an outline version of the Medium weight too.  

I wound up with four members of the Alimentary family, each with over 700 glyphs!  Not only do they all have the basics (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, and tons of punctuation), but they also each have 330 characters for European language support, and a limited selection of Greek, Coptic, and Cyrillic characters.  Plus a double handful of alternates and ligatures to add a little variety to your designs!

Alga is a high-contrast modern typeface with a contemporary look. It has subtle details that make it appealing for big sizes and headlines. It is a lively and charming serif typeface with lots of fancy curves. It is a serif typeface that will shine in headlines and short pieces of text. The italic is lively and with stronger corners cutting a bit of the sweetness of the upright style.  You will make your headlines shine using Alga.

Alegria is a font family designed for joyful communication. The family is comprised of Alegria Roman (with upper/lowercase and oldstyle figures), Alegria Caps (with uppercase, small caps and lining figures), Alegria Bright (a small caps version with a three-dimensional feel) and Alegria Fill (that can be used as a second layer with Bright or Caps faces to create multiple colors on the text). Alegria family is suitable for short display texts and can be used in many ways you can creatively think of.

Aldero™ strives to be as useful to any design environment as Alder trees are to the forest. To achieve what we set out to do, we gave Aldero™ the two-in-one looks, virtually doubled the sets of glyphs and ligatures, and loaded it with plenty more Opentype features. And we truly believe that you will enjoy working with this typeface as much as we do. 

With 5 weights, 10 styles, and 1,100+ glyphs per style, this versatile typeface boasts virtually two looks. The standard glyph set is perfect for formal, corporate design, while the stylistic alternate set elicits a fun, friendly, and casual feel. You can use each style separately or mix and match them to achieve your design aesthetic.
Alder Road an ultra-condensed serif face in the Didone tradition, but with some playful art nouveau details scattered throughout.

Alchemy is a single weight decorative type drawing its inspiration from the lettering style of the Middle Ages. The character set allows you to craft and tailor individual words and phrases. There are several different designs of each letter and even those that sport only one design can be modified through the included plug-in elements. Superior and inferior letters are designed to fit between the core letter shapes and can be used to add another degree of finesse. A set of pre-built ligatures provide additional visual patterning as do the joining letter versions of C and A. Used in combination with the finial and linking elements makes endless possibilities to become a digital scribe.

A rounded version of Albiona, a contemporary slab-serif which revisits aspects of Robert Besley’s classic Clarendon. Originally named after the Clarendon Press in Oxford, the type family was subsequently extended by Stephenson Blake in the 1950s.

Albiona adds the inwardly-curved stroke terminals of the same foundry’s Grotesque series, and includes italics and old-style and tabular numerals. The original Clarendon’s ball serifs and calligraphic eccentricities have been rationalised for functional contemporary uses. The family consists of five weights plus italics and a stencil, and its clean readable style is perfect for both extended text as well as headline setting.

A contemporary slab-serif which revisits aspects of Robert Besley’s all-time classic Clarendon, designed around 1842 for Thorowgood and Co. and named after the Clarendon Press in Oxford. The original design was subsequently extended by Sheffield foundry Stephenson Blake in the 1950s into a widely-used, robust workhorse family.

Albiona uses the inwardly curved stroke terminals of the same foundry’s Grotesque series, while rationalising or removing entirely Clarendon’s ball serifs, flicked tails and other eccentricities to make it more functional in contemporary settings. Bring some sass to your signage! Alasassy is a font inspired from Sharpie pen drawings, featuring ink ball terminals. The Caps version features a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters that share the same cap height and baseline. There are several alternate characters with a mix of high and low crossbars as well as crossbar overhang options and language support for each. The Pro versions include Greek and Cyrillic. 

This display font will bring some zest to your logo, signage, packaging design or large titles on book covers or advertising. It is a great combination of an organic, hand drawn feel but still clean and crisp enough to look professional. Enjoy!

Aktaion stands in the tradition of the humanistic design approach. Because I strongly believe that this offers the best reading comfort in the sanserif genre.
Aktaion consists of 8 weights plus their corresponding italics. It covers all Latin script based languages, comes with OpenType feature sets as e. g. for tabular, proportional lining or small figures (the default figures are proportional lining figures), for uppercase variants, for arbitrary fractions or for full lowercase superior & inferior letters & figures.
The letters are detailed with contrasting sharp edges and rounded corners, with stems having one straight side and one side with a concave shape resulting in a gripping tension.

Airco is a typeface designed with italic and script styles at its core. The letterforms have a rounded finishing. Airco is designed at an ultra slanted (27°), where the shapes evoke a fast and assertive movement; this result in a human and dynamic typeface. Airco works visually well in technology and sport, yet it eliminates any dryness, rigidity or inhumanity. The letters structure is influenced by Renaissance italics, however, the lowercase and capitals are visually homogeneous (thanks to the giant lowercase). In fact, the default numerals can be used in both capital and lowercase settings.

Aiglon is a monolinear, semi-grotesque, semi-geometric sans serif. It is an open face, very sober yet recognisable, thanks to its unique characteristics. As it might be obvious by now, the idea behind Aiglon is to reaffirm French style within European heritage. Aiglon is directly influenced from lettering tradition. The success of grotesques from the end of the 19th century might unintentionally assert a local style: a detail might immediately refer to a Latin style, while another more English or Germanic. Asserting instead the mono-linearity of the style, there is no super heavy weights. The italics are drawn narrower than the romans in order to contrast. Aiglon is available in five widths.

As it might be obvious by now, the idea behind Aiglon is to reaffirm French style within European heritage. Aiglon is directly influenced from lettering tradition. The success of grotesques from the end of the 19th century might unintentionally assert a local style: a detail might immediately refer to a Latin style, while another more English or Germanic. Asserting instead the mono-linearity of the style, there is no super heavy weights. The italics are drawn narrower than the romans in order to contrast. Aiglon is available in five widths.

Roundness is the heart of Aglet Slab’s structure—not merely a surface detail. Blunt serifs and repeated geometric shapes find variety in a strategic hierarchy of curves, from subtly cushioned points to abrupt circular ends. An underlying framework of 45° and 90° angles provides a stable foundation for more boastful characters and organic details.

Aglet Slab reverberates a friendly high-tech tone when used prominently, but it stays crisp and nimble in longer texts. A broad range of weights in roman and italic add up to fourteen versatile styles, each with matching symbols. You’ll want Aglet Slab at hand for whatever comes around the corner.

At once technical and human, Aglet Sans explores what it means to be round, and the ways in which a system can be implemented and strategically broken. A lively mix of corner radiuses offsets strict modular structures. Interlocking entrance and exit strokes create spirited counterforms that urge the eye forward. These unorthodox details generate interest when set large, yet provide a crisp but unobtrusive voice for paragraphs and captions, both in print and on screen.

Easily at home in editorial heads and decks, the Aglet superfamily will also add buoyant personality to corporate branding systems, interfaces, and environmental graphics.

Round architecture informs Aglet Mono, tempering its rigorous, fixed-width rhythm. Clever strategies offset the lopsided spatial artifacts produced by a monospaced design: the dented sides of A, V, W, v, and w compensate for the absence of kerning. Extroverted f, j, r, and t fill their allotted space with curious hooks, and a brazen g supports the calculated weirdness of some of the other glyphs. 

A display face at heart, Aglet Mono also translates well to the more intimate, routine demands of code. Its atmosphere is distinctly industrial and technical, but also unstudied and ad hoc. Aglet Mono is a typeface for people who make stuff, whether headlines or software.

As an interpretation and further development of the original source, Aeroplan now has eight styles (four uprights with italics) designed for paragraph text, with another ten Titling styles that will be released later this year to complete the family. The text styles are robust, enjoy a healthy dose of contrast, and contain functional inktraps for rendering in print as pristine and on screen as unique. Aeroplan’s perfect use would be in contemporary magazines or books about art, engineering, or architecture, newspaper text, and even more edgy and obscure subjects. Anywhere Baskerville could be used, replace it with Aeroplan for an immediate update and texture improvement in paragraphs.

Adrianna is a fashionable yet restrained sans-serif font family for sophisticated designs. It’s a smart and versatile family of fonts, comprised of 30 styles across a range of three widths. The Regular width is a plain and clear heavy-lifting font. The Extended variety is meant to look good on tv and other wide format output media. And the proportions of the Condensed makes it looks especially good when seen on a smartphone.

It’s a legible and direct type family. Ranging in  weights (plus italics) from Thin to Extrabold in each width style, Adrianna has enough flavors to allow the finicky designer a broad typographic palette to work with.

What can be more lovely than a wedding, an intimate invitation, a gift from the heart? One whose presentation uses the warm and welcoming family of typefaces, Adorn. With a modern and sometimes quirky twist on the staid, almost corporate look of formal invitations, this family of lettering typefaces arms designers with a breathtakingly large number of faces that work harmoniously, despite the distinctiveness of each. Even larger and more multilayered than Worthington’s award-winning Charcuterie collection, Adorn offers seven display fonts, four script designs, monograms, ornaments, illustrations, banners, frames, and catchwords.

Adore Mono is a monospaced font with a split personality. Playful, yet slightly ominous.

A humanist sans serif that falls in the “evil (sans) serif” genre, especially designed for contemporary typography and comes up with 7 weights from extralight to black plus true italics and 293 ligatures and initial letters. A large x-height not only creates space in the letters for extra-bold styles, but also lends Ador Hairline an open and generous character in the more narrow and semi-bold versions. The nice balance between sharp ink trapped and soft, dynamic shapes helps to work in small sizes. Diagonal stress, angled finials and the 4 degree true italic styles give Ador Hairline a dynamic look.
Ador Hairline was on the shortlist of Communication Arts 2020

Ador is a humanist sans serif especially designed for contemporary typography and comes up with 8 weights from ultralight to black plus true italics and 343 ligatures.
A large x-height not only creates space in the letters for extra-bold styles, but also lends Ador an open and generous character in the more narrow and semi-bold versions. The nice balance between sharp ink trapped and soft, dynamic shapes helps to work in small sizes. Diagonal stress, angled finials  give Ador a dynamic look.
The font contains 981 glyphs including small caps, tabular, old style, fractions … and a wide range of flexibility for Latin language support for every typographical needs.

A versatile humanist sans-serif font family with a slight touch of flavor, can be described as a true battle horse in the realm of typography, adaptable to a wide range of uses. 
Whether it's crafting elegant editorial layouts, establishing a strong corporative identity, or creating captivating web designs, Adia Pro's extensive weight variations and italics provide designers with the perfect tools to emphasize text as needed, ensuring readability and visual impact in any context.
Moreover, its comprehensive coverage of Latin European and Cyrillic scripts makes it an excellent choice for global projects. 
Adia was selected for the ninth Tipos Latinos Biennal 2022 in Super Family category.

This version covers Cyrillic Scrip, covering languages as Russian, Serbian, Macedonian, Belarusian, Ukranian and Bulgarian.

Adelphi is an approachable geometric sans-serif influenced by the British modernist tradition. The contemporary, comprehensive and durable type system comes with a pragmatic set of features including a wide array of weights and ‘duplex italics’. Variable extenders go from tall and flat in Adelphi Text to short and sharp in Adelphi Display, with default Adelphi standing midway between these two extremes. This understated beauty supports Latin, Cyrillic, and Greek scripts and comes with a large number of alternates, fractions and arrows.

Twenty styles designed with both the developer and the aesthete in mind, the Adelle Mono family has a true monospaced width (Mono), a proportional width (Flex), and a variable font that modulates between the two to boost creativity and coherence.

Adelbrook is a dynamic serif typeface that keeps calm. It enriches text with the archaic structure of humanist type. Its characters arrange in a harmonious rhythm with asymmetric serifs and forward-leaning stems. A heaviness is defined by tapered stems that emphasize foot serifs. These characters have gravity and are firmly on the baseline. Actually all the details are heftier the lower they are. Therefore you find a subtle vertical hairline variation, light or unapplied head serifs and clipped upper dots.

The clearness of the semi-serif italics with a brushy nature integrates perfectly. All these details result in a sophisticated text typeface with a sharp contemporary design.

name: Adapter PE Text
authors: David Březina, William Montrose, Sláva Jevčinová

raw.designer: David Březina, William Montrose, Sláva Jevčinová
raw.description: Adapter is a universal sans-serif typeface with contemporary aesthetics, a straightforward typeface that is easy to use for a wide range of design genres. Two size-specific variants, Text and Display, come together in a type system that packs a wide range of weights and even the duplexed italics into a single,lightweight variable font. The Adapter superfamily currently supports Arabic, Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, and Latin.

Adapt spans five widths from Normal to Compressed and eight weights from Thin to Black plus lots of handy extras. An overall flexible playground for typographic expression with a total of 80 fonts to choose from. Even more choice comes with Adapt’s 2 variable fonts, Adapt Var Roman and Italic, that allow for a seamless navigation within the design parameters of width and weight. The usual styles can be chosen at any time as well.
Acorn is a display sans serif in seven weights. It's clean and modern, but with some organic touches for a unique typographic flow. Variable font included with purchase of the full family.

Accent Graphic was developed as the corporate font for a London design consultancy in 1997. The starting point was the word ‘accent’ in lower case.
Accent Graphic is essentially a sans typeface with the thick/thin contrast of a serif and is the only font family in the G-Type retail collection that was originally designed for a client.
Flared stems and graceful strokes make Accent Graphic a delicately beautiful typeface with broad appeal.
The family consists of three weights (Light, Medium & Bold), available in OpenType format with support for Western and Central European languages.

An extension to the award-winning Abril font family, Abril Titling’s letter shapes remain sturdy, very legible, and carry a newsy feel. Some details have been ironed out for improved performance in print and screen headlines, making Abril Titling a stylish workhorse font family that maintains high impact.

The Abril font family is a credible, contemporary interpretation of a classic newsface and was conceived for intensive editorial use in newspapers, magazines, and digital media. The Display styles have a strong presence and a newsy feel on the page while the Text styles were engineered from scratch to achieve the right colour, texture, and overall width for comfortable, continuous reading in printed and digital environments.

This typeface comes from a self initiated project which aims to contribute to keep a group of minority languages alive through solving issues in the education environment, called Sápmi.

This re-thought edition takes the name of Aanaar and joins our library with a bigger character set and two new weights which complete the typeface providing a big typographic palette as well as adding stylistic two-story a and g for more advanced readers as well as to enable the type-face to be used in other environments.
